Usage

Robust-PCA low-rank (background) part.

Decomposes the image matrix M into M = L + S (low-rank L + sparse S) by solving Principal Component Pursuit with inexact ALM (Lin/Chen/Ma 2010), and returns L. The weight of the sparse term is λ = (0.5 + 1.5*a) / sqrt(max(m, n)) (m, n are the matrix dimensions at decomposition); the larger a, the sparser S, and correspondingly the components (rank) remaining in L increase. At a=0, λ is small, most of the variation is absorbed into S, and L becomes featureless. b is unused. At most 60 iterations, with the convergence test ||M - L - S||_F <= 1e-7 * ||M||_F.

Images whose longer side exceeds 64 are downscaled to 64 for decomposition, and only L is brought back to the original size by linear interpolation (because the low-rank part tolerates downscaling). The input is brought to 2-D float64 in [0,1] (3-D is channel-averaged); the return value has the same shape, clipped to [0,1]. An all-zero image returns the input unchanged. The number of BLAS threads is limited with fsthreads only during decomposition (for SVD of small matrices, more threads are slower). On exception it is fail-soft: a clipped version of the input is returned and recorded in the ledger.

Since this decomposition treats "structure repeating across rows and columns" (stripes, gradients, periodic patterns) as background, even for a single 2-D image it is well suited to separating isolated defects from periodic backgrounds such as fabric, sheets or display pixels. On non-periodic backgrounds like natural images, L is merely a low-rank approximation and does not become a meaningful background. The paired defect side is dc_rpca_sparse (L + (S - 0.5) == input). To extract structure with edge-preserving smoothing, use dc_structure_texture.
